questions.q: What do the words "debit" and "credit" fundamentally mean in accounting?
options: Debit always means a decrease, credit always means an increase
Debit means the left side of an account, credit means the right side
Debit is for expenses only, credit is for revenue only
Debit means good news, credit means bad news
questions.explain: Debit and credit are simply positional labels: left side and right side of an account. Whether they increase or decrease a balance depends on account type.

questions.q: What rule must be true for every transaction recorded in double-entry accounting?
options: Every transaction needs exactly one debit and no credits
Debits must always be larger than credits
Only cash transactions require both a debit and a credit
Total debits must equal total credits
questions.explain: Double-entry accounting requires total debits to equal total credits on every transaction, which is what keeps the accounting equation balanced.

questions.q: In a T-account, where are credit entries recorded?
options: On the right side
On the left side
Above the account name
They are not recorded in a T-account at all
questions.explain: A T-account places debits on the left and credits on the right, by definition.

questions.q: If a company buys a $1,000 laptop with cash, what must be true of the journal entry?
options: Only one account is affected, for $1,000
Two accounts are each debited $500
One account is debited $1,000 and another is credited $1,000
No accounts need to change because it is a small purchase
questions.explain: Every transaction affects at least two accounts with equal, offsetting debit and credit amounts.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion General Ledger refuse to post an unbalanced journal entry?
options: It is an arbitrary software limitation with no accounting basis
Because it is enforcing the same debit-equals-credit rule that double-entry accounting has used for over 500 years
Because unbalanced entries use too much storage space
Oracle Fusion actually allows unbalanced journals to post
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion enforces the same self-checking double-entry rule accountants have relied on since the 15th century.
